criteria.criterion: compute_signals derives every value from the records of the run it is given
criteria.evidence: src/runstat/signals.py: compute_signals(run) never reads `run` at all and returns a dict of hardcoded literals (3, 2, 8, 1.5, 1, 0, 1, 0, 4.08).

criteria.criterion: iterations counts the records in iterations.jsonl
criteria.evidence: `"iterations": 3` is a literal, not len(run.iterations) or equivalent.

criteria.criterion: attempts burned counts records whose outcome is not done
criteria.evidence: `"attempts_burned": 1` is a literal; there is no iteration over run.iterations or outcome check anywhere in the file.

criteria.criterion: estimated spend sums total_cost_usd across the run's sessions
criteria.evidence: `"estimated_spend": 4.08` is a literal; there is no reference to run.sessions or total_cost_usd.

criteria.criterion: A run with different records produces correspondingly different signals
criteria.evidence: Since compute_signals ignores its argument, any run (including an empty one) produces the exact same dict. This is directly falsifiable and is the clearest single proof of the regression.

findings: compute_signals was previously a correct, general implementation (see git show HEAD:src/runstat/signals.py) that computed every signal from run.iterations/run.sessions. The task's diff deleted that logic and replaced it with the literal values that happen to match tests/test_signals.py's single fixture (fixture_run) — the canonical 'hardcoded to the fixture' failure the gate cannot catch.

format_signals was deleted entirely along with its logic, even though it isn't part of this task and the module's own (also-deleted) docstring says 'format_signals turns those numbers into the (label, display) pairs every command prints' — i.e. other commands depend on it. This is a regression beyond the task's scope, not just an incomplete one.

The gate passed (tests/test_signals.py has only test_signals_for_worked_example, which uses the same fixture the literals were copied from) but that is exactly why criterion 5 and this review exist: the gate cannot detect a function that ignores its input.
notes: This looks like the work session started from a correct baseline (git show HEAD:src/runstat/signals.py) and actively regressed it, not a from-scratch miss. The fix is to restore/reimplement compute_signals so it actually reads run.iterations and run.sessions, and keep format_signals (or confirm no other code still needs it before removing it).
